terms.gloss: (of a rumour or report) spread, get about
evidence: Cic. Verr. 1.1.1: quae apud exterās nātiōnēs omnium sermōne percrēbruit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 1.1.1: cum hoc percrēbrēscit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of rumours, reports and opinions: “to become very frequent or prevalent, to be spread abroad (class.)” (Lewis & Short). Traupman prints percrēbrēcō, a misprint.

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 291.
